findings.title: Inline directive appended to slash command may be parsed as part of the command arguments
findings.why: The old _build_prompt returns a slash command string like '/sc:reflect --mode post --diff abc123'. The new code appends a multi-line natural-language directive to this command string. However, slash command parsers typically treat everything on the same line or contiguous block as part of the command. The appended directive starts with '\n\n' which creates separation, but there's no evidence in the codebase that the /sc:reflect command processor distinguishes between command flags (parsed) and trailing natural-language directives (preserved as instructions). If the skill's argument parser is strict, the appended text could be rejected as invalid flags or silently truncated.
findings.recommendation: Verify that the /sc:reflect skill protocol explicitly supports trailing natural-language instructions after the flag list, or use a documented directive format (e.g., a recognized flag like --execution-mode inline or a structured comment). If unsupported, the directive will be ignored and the fix will have no effect.

findings.title: Missing test coverage for the appended inline-execution directive
findings.why: The change modifies the return value of _build_prompt by appending a directive. Existing tests (test_o1_default_prompt_omits_no_promote, test_o2_no_promote_prompt_contains_no_promote) verify flag presence in the prompt string, but there's no test verifying that the appended directive (a) is present in the built prompt, (b) is correctly formatted, or (c) actually changes the execution path when consumed by the skill. Without tests, regressions (e.g., f-string escaping issues, directive truncation, or no-op behavior) won't be caught.
findings.recommendation: Add a test that asserts the inline directive is present in _build_prompt() output and an integration test that verifies the directive changes execution mode (e.g., by checking that Tier-2 reviewers spawn as direct subagents of the top-level orchestrator, not nested workers). Verify the directive survives the ClaudeProcess stdin write (process.py:205) without truncation.

findings.title: Prompt construction change not reflected in dry-run preview method
findings.why: The dry-run / print-command path (lines 465-478) calls _build_prompt() and prints the result at line 467. The appended directive will appear in the dry-run output, but the comment at line 461 ('Build the slash prompt') and the dry-run's print statement context suggest this is intended to show the command flags only, not the full prompt with natural-language directives. Users running --print-command may be confused by the multi-line directive appearing in what looks like a command-line invocation.
findings.recommendation: Update the dry-run output to clearly distinguish between the slash command (flags) and the appended directive, or add a comment explaining that the printed prompt includes execution directives. Alternatively, provide a --print-command-only flag that omits directives for scripting use cases.

findings.title: Directive text is not parameterized or localized
findings.evidence:
inline_directive = (
            "\n\nExecute this reflect run INLINE, yourself, as the top-level orchestrator. "...
findings.why: The directive is a multi-line string literal hardcoded inline. Best practice for this type of instruction is to define it as a module-level constant (e.g., _INLINE_EXECUTION_DIRECTIVE) so it can be reused, tested independently, and easily modified. The inline placement makes it harder to unit-test the directive text (e.g., verify it contains no f-string injection risks, matches expected wording) and harder to locate when debugging.
findings.recommendation: Extract the directive to a module-level constant: _INLINE_EXECUTION_DIRECTIVE = "\n\nExecute this reflect run INLINE..." and reference it in _build_prompt. This improves testability and makes the directive discoverable via grep.

findings.title: No validation that directive prevents nested delegation
findings.evidence: "Do NOT delegate the whole run to a subagent. When the protocol reaches Wave 3..."
findings.why: The comment at lines 11-15 states the directive is intended to prevent the reflect run from delegating into a worker subagent, which would degrade to single-reviewer because callbacks route to the coordinator. However, there's no evidence that the sc-reflect-protocol skill respects natural-language directives in this way. The protocol SKILL.md (lines 51-56) lists triggers and auto-activation rules but doesn't document a directive-based execution-mode override. If the skill ignores the directive or interprets it as advisory rather than mandatory, the fix will have no effect.
findings.recommendation: Cross-reference the sc-reflect-protocol SKILL.md to confirm that natural-language directives after the flag list are parsed and enforced. If not, propose a formal flag (e.g., --inline-execution) or ensure the directive format matches a documented convention (e.g., markdown-style directives in skill input). Add an integration test that verifies callbacks from Wave 3 reviewers are collected by the top-level orchestrator.

cross_cutting_observations.title: Slash command prompt construction lacks a documented contract for natural-language directives
cross_cutting_observations.why: The change assumes that appending natural-language instructions after the slash command flags will be honored by the skill. However, the skill protocol documentation (SKILL.md §3.1, commands/reflect.md §3) specifies only flag-based inputs (--mode, --diff, --tasklist, etc.) with no mention of trailing natural-language directives. The sc-reflect-protocol SKILL.md §4 Wave 0 step 0.1 says 'Parse flags + apply §3.2 mode-selection' but doesn't reference directive parsing. Without a documented contract for how directives are parsed vs. flags, this change is fragile: upstream changes to the skill's argument parser could silently break the fix.
cross_cutting_observations.recommendation: Establish a documented contract for slash command prompts that includes both structured flags and optional natural-language directives. Update the sc-reflect-protocol SKILL.md to explicitly state that natural-language text after the flag list is preserved as execution instructions. Alternatively, formalize the directive as a --execution-mode flag or a recognized comment format.

cross_cutting_observations.title: No integration test verifying the end-to-end callback routing fix
cross_cutting_observations.why: The PR description states the change fixes a degradation where Tier-2 reviewer callbacks route to the top-level coordinator instead of back to a nested runner. This is a complex distributed behavior involving ClaudeProcess spawning, skill execution, and callback routing. None of the existing tests in tests/cli/reflect/ verify callback routing or multi-reviewer ensemble behavior. Without an integration test that spawns a reflect run and verifies that Wave 3 reviewers return results to the top-level orchestrator (not a nested worker), the fix cannot be validated.
cross_cutting_observations.recommendation: Add an integration test that mocks or runs a full reflect run with --depth deep, verifies that multiple Tier-2 reviewers spawn as direct subagents of the top-level process (not nested), and confirms that their results are collected in the return-contract.yaml. Use process mocking to verify the prompt passed to ClaudeProcess includes the directive and that the resulting tier_reached >= 2.

notes_for_orchestrator: The change appends a natural-language directive to the /sc:reflect prompt, but the skill protocol documentation does not explicitly support this pattern. The fix may be no-op if the directive is ignored. Recommend verifying that the sc-reflect-protocol skill parses and honors trailing natural-language instructions, or propose a formal flag-based approach. Test coverage is absent for both the directive's presence in the prompt and its effect on execution path.
